lead: The densest neighbourhood in Barcelona, a short step from Sants station.
text: With 25,243 inhabitants in just 0.41 km², Sants-Badal is the most densely populated neighbourhood in the city, with about 60,827 inhabitants per km². Its name comes from the Rambla de Badal, and historically it was part of Sants, although the city's new territorial division gave it neighbourhood status in its own right. The amendment to the general plan for the area around Rambla de Badal and the Jardins de la Rambla de Sants, given initial approval in November 2025, sets aside 5,000 m² of land for public facilities; final approval is still pending.

Avinguda de Madrid and the Rambla de Badal are its landmarks, and to one side lies the Riera Blanca, which marks the boundary with L'Hospitalet. Its density shows in well-lived streets, with blocks of flats, local shops and everything within walking distance, and it keeps its neighbourhood ties with the rest of Sants. If you are selling, the average sale price (3,958 €/m² in 2025) is practically in line with the Sants-Montjuïc average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 317,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sants-Montjuïc (5th of 8 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (943 €/month) is 6% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats on densely populated streets, with plenty of local shops.
